common.metadata: Metadata only: names, e-mails, roles, two-factor state and session timestamps. Never session tokens, IP addresses, user agents or end-user data.

errors.forbidden: Your platform role does not allow this action.
errors.confirm_required: Confirm the action in the dialog first.
errors.not_found: No account with this address or id.
errors.self: You cannot change your own platform role — another platform admin has to.
errors.unchanged: The account already has this role.
errors.lastAdmin: This is the last platform admin; grant the admin role to someone else first.
errors.emailNotVerified: The account has not verified its e-mail address; a platform role is granted to verified accounts only.
errors.ticketRequired: You are the only admin who can decide this change: a ticket reference is required for a self-approved change.
errors.needsThirdAdmin: A second platform admin exists but cannot decide a change to their own role. Grant the admin role to a third person first, or use the ops:grant command.
errors.duplicate: A role change for this account is already waiting for a decision.
errors.fourEyes: You filed this request; a different platform admin has to apply it (four eyes).
errors.stale: The account’s role changed since the request was filed; decline it and file a new one.
errors.expired: The request expired; file a new one.
errors.notOperator: Sessions are revoked for platform operators only; the customer directory is read-only.
errors.generic: The action failed. Try again; the failure has been recorded.
errors.selfTwoFactor: You cannot reset your own two-factor authentication — another platform admin has to.
errors.notEnabled: Two-factor is not enabled for this account; there is nothing to reset.
errors.organizationRequired: Choose the organisation the support ticket belongs to.
errors.notMember: The account is not a member of that organisation.

notices.proposed: Request filed. A different platform admin has to apply it; it expires after seven days.
notices.applied: Role changed and recorded as self-approved. {count, plural, =0 {No stored sessions to revoke.} one {# session revoked.} other {# sessions revoked.}}
notices.approved: Role changed. {count, plural, =0 {No stored sessions to revoke.} one {# session revoked.} other {# sessions revoked.}}
notices.sessionsRevoked: {count, plural, =0 {No stored sessions to revoke.} one {# session revoked.} other {# sessions revoked.}} The account has to sign in again.
notices.twoFactorReset: Two-factor reset: secret and backup codes deleted. {count, plural, =0 {No stored sessions to revoke.} one {# session revoked.} other {# sessions revoked.}} {mailed, select, yes {The person has been notified by e-mail.} other {The notification e-mail could not be sent — inform the person another way.}}

overview.intro: Accounts with a platform role, their two-factor state and sessions, and the four-eyes rule for granting roles. Customer accounts are listed read-only in the directory.

rules.title: Four-eyes status
rules.admins: {eligible} of {total, plural, one {# platform admin} other {# platform admins}} can decide requests.
rules.eligibleHint: Deciding admins have a verified e-mail{twoFactor, select, yes { and two-factor enabled} other {}}.
rules.on: A role change you file is applied by a different platform admin.
rules.off: You are the only deciding admin: role changes you file are applied at once, recorded as self-approved, and need a ticket reference.
rules.bootstrap: The first platform admin is granted with the ops:grant command; from then on roles change here.
rules.signOut: Every role change deletes the account’s stored sessions (forced sign-out). A cached session can stay valid for up to {minutes} minutes.

requests.title: Pending role changes
requests.intro: Requests wait here until a different platform admin applies or declines them. They expire after seven days.
requests.caption: Role change requests with account, change, reason, proposer and available decisions
requests.staleHint: The account’s role changed meanwhile ({role}); this request can only be declined.

cannot.fourEyes: You filed this request — another admin applies it.

dialog.approveText: {from} → {to}. The account is signed out everywhere and the change is recorded with both admins in the audit log.
dialog.declineText: Nothing changes for the account; the decision is recorded in the audit log.
dialog.withdrawText: Nothing changes for the account; the withdrawal is recorded in the audit log.
dialog.reasonHint: Optional, up to {max} characters; stored in the audit log.

operators.title: Operators
operators.caption: Accounts with a platform role, their two-factor and verification state, last sign-in, active sessions and available actions
operators.emptyText: Grant the first platform admin with the ops:grant command; further roles are granted here.
operators.memberOf: {count, plural, one {Member of # organisation} other {Member of # organisations}}
operators.activeSessions: {count, plural, =0 {none active} one {# active} other {# active}}
operators.self: Your own account: another admin changes your role.
operators.lastAdmin: Last platform admin: cannot be demoted.
operators.selfTwoFactor: Your own account: another admin resets your two-factor.

roleDialog.title: Change the platform role of {name}
roleDialog.grantDescription: The person signs up as a normal user and verifies the e-mail first; then the role is granted here.
roleDialog.emailHint: Exact address of an existing, verified account.
roleDialog.reasonHint: At least {min} characters, up to {max}. Stored in the audit log.
roleDialog.ticketHint: For example OPS-1234. Required when no other admin can decide (self-approved change).
roleDialog.modeProposal: Four eyes: this files a request that a different platform admin applies.
roleDialog.modeSelf: You are the only admin who can decide: the change is applied at once, recorded as self-approved, and needs a ticket reference.
roleDialog.signOut: The account is signed out everywhere when the change is applied.

revokeDialog.title: Sign out {name} everywhere?
revokeDialog.text: Every stored session of the account is deleted; the person has to sign in again (with two-factor). The action is recorded in the audit log.
revokeDialog.selfWarning: This is your own account: you will be signed out too.
revokeDialog.cache: A cached session can stay valid for up to {minutes} minutes.
revokeDialog.reasonHint: At least {min} characters; stored in the audit log.

history.title: Recent role changes
history.intro: The newest {count} role entries of the audit log — requests, applied changes (console and CLI), declines and withdrawals.
history.caption: Recent role-change audit entries with time, actor, action, account and change
history.sessionsRevoked: {count, plural, one {# session revoked} other {# sessions revoked}}

directory.title: Customer directory
directory.intro: Every account with its organisations and roles, two-factor state, creation and last sign-in — read-only metadata, no end-user data.
directory.countFiltered: {count, plural, one {# matching account} other {# matching accounts}}
directory.caption: Accounts with memberships, roles, two-factor and verification state, last sign-in and creation date
directory.emptyText: Accounts appear here as soon as the first person signs up.
directory.emptyFilteredText: Loosen the filters or clear the search.
directory.methods: Last sign-in: newest stored session (rows vanish on sign-out and clean-up, so “no stored session” does not mean the person never signed in). Active: sessions that have not expired.

profile.passkeys: {count, plural, =0 {No passkeys} one {# passkey} other {# passkeys}}
profile.customer: Customer account without platform role: read-only here.

memberships.caption: Organisations the account belongs to with role and join date

sessions.caption: Stored sessions of the account with sign-in, last activity, expiry, state and active organisation
sessions.summary: {active, plural, one {# active session} other {# active sessions}} · {expired, plural, one {# expired} other {# expired}}
sessions.truncated: The {count} most recent sessions are shown.
sessions.noSecrets: Session tokens, IP addresses and user agents are never shown here.

audit.caption: Audit entries targeting this account with time, actor, action and redacted details
audit.empty: No audit entries for this account.
audit.limit: The {count} most recent entries are shown; the Audit module has the full log.

twoFactorDialog.title: Reset two-factor for {name}?
twoFactorDialog.text: The authenticator secret and the backup codes are deleted, two-factor is switched off and every stored session is revoked. The person signs in with the password only and sets up two-factor again; they are notified by e-mail in their language.
twoFactorDialog.operatorHint: Track Operations requires two-factor: the operator is locked out of the console until two-factor is set up again.
twoFactorDialog.customerHint: Support tool for a customer account: reason and ticket reference are mandatory; the entry is recorded with the ticket’s organisation and shows in that organisation’s audit log.
twoFactorDialog.reasonHint: At least {min} characters, up to {max}. Stored in the audit log.
twoFactorDialog.ticketHint: For example SUP-1234. Mandatory for customer accounts.
twoFactorDialog.ticketOptionalHint: For example OPS-1234. Optional for platform operators.
twoFactorDialog.organisationHint: The organisation the ticket belongs to; the audit entry is recorded there.
twoFactorDialog.notice: Recorded in the audit log with actor, account, reason and ticket — never the secret or the backup codes.
